content.definition: Information material if omission or misstatement could influence economic decisions of users
content.fasb_definition: Magnitude of omission/misstatement that makes it probable judgment of reasonable person would have been changed or influenced
content.key_principle: Materiality is relative, not absolute. Depends on size AND nature of item in context.

quantitative_guidelines.context_matters: Small amount may be material if affects trends, key ratios, or regulatory compliance

qualitative_factors: Effect on debt covenants or regulatory requirements
Potential for aggregation with other misstatements

materiality_contexts.financial_statement_level: Overall materiality for financial statements as whole
materiality_contexts.account_level: Performance materiality for specific accounts (set lower)
materiality_contexts.disclosure_level: Whether item requires disclosure in notes
materiality_contexts.error_correction: Whether error significant enough to require restatement

quantitatively_small_but_qualitatively_m: Small adjustment that turns loss into profit
Small amount that causes debt covenant violation
Expense misclassified to wrong period to meet analyst expectations
Related party transaction (even if small amount)

aggregation.principle: Individual immaterial items may be material in aggregate
aggregation.evaluation: Consider cumulative effect of all adjustments/misstatements

intentional_misstatements.fraud: Even small amounts material if intentional (qualitative materiality)
intentional_misstatements.sec_guidance: Intentional misstatements not immaterial regardless of amount

disclosure_materiality.separate_assessment: Item immaterial for recognition may be material for disclosure
disclosure_materiality.example: Small related party transaction may not affect amounts but should be disclosed

materiality_vs_conservatism.conservatism: Prefer understatement to overstatement when uncertain
materiality_vs_conservatism.relationship: Materiality allows practical expedients; conservatism applies to material judgments

audit_context.planning_materiality: Auditor sets materiality level for audit planning
audit_context.performance_materiality: Lower threshold for testing specific accounts (allows for aggregation)
audit_context.misstatement_evaluation: Uncorrected misstatements evaluated against materiality thresholds

examples_immaterial: Small clerical errors with no effect on decisions
Immaterial classification errors (if not affecting key ratios)
examples_material: Error changing profit to loss (even if small $ amount)
Misstatement affecting key performance indicators or trends
cpa_exam_tips: Materiality = relative, not absolute (depends on context)
Quantitative: Often 5-10% of net income or 1-2% of assets
Qualitative factors equally important (nature, fraud, covenants, trends)
Small amount can be material if qualitatively significant
Aggregate immaterial items may be material in total

key_points: Materiality: Information material if could influence user decisions
Relative concept (depends on size AND nature in context)
Quantitative guidelines: 5-10% NI, 1-2% assets, but not absolute
Qualitative factors: Fraud, trends, covenants, motivation
Aggregate effect: Immaterial items may be material in total
